note: The why names the two sounds to listen for (IV moves away, V pulls back), so the learner can use it on any song. Each block turns the same listening drill a new way: two chords at a time, all three with the answer hidden (and again in D from the Key row), then chords that stay two bars so counting no longer works. The band is named the same way in every step.

exercise.title: Hear the 4 and the 5 coming
exercise.focus: I IV V by ear · G and D major, then A · guess before you look
exercise.why: The IV chord moves away from home and the V chord pulls back towards it, so once you know those two sounds you can tell which chord is playing in any song.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the band: G and C take turns, then G and D. Watch the lit chord box and listen for how C moves away from G and how D pulls back to it. Call out 4 on every C and 5 on every D.

Press Play below to start the band: all three chords now, in a new order. Look away from the chord boxes and call out 1, 4 or 5 on each change, then look to check. When you hear it before you think it, tap D in the Key row above the band and guess again. The chords change, the pull doesn't.

Press Play below to start the band, now in A. Some chords stay for two bars, so you can't count your way to the next change: look away and call out the number only when you hear the chord move. Then put on a song you know and listen for the 4 and the 5.
